quests.name: Amulet of the Moon
quests.plugin: Skyrim.esm (no other plugin edits the quest)
quests.canDoWhy: Kharjo, a guard with one of the Khajiit caravans, wants his Moon Amulet back from a dungeon.

starts.where: with Ahkari's Khajiit caravan, near wherever its camp is
starts.how: Speak with Kharjo; the quest sends you to find his Moon Amulet in a dungeon and bring it back to him.

quests.firstStep: Find the Moon Amulet inside the dungeon

takesYou.place: a dungeon the game picks when the quest starts
back to Kharjo at the caravan

objectives: Find the Moon Amulet inside the dungeon
Return the Moon Amulet to Kharjo

people.name: Kharjo
people.role: quest giver; a guard travelling with Ahkari's Khajiit caravan; listed as someone who can become a follower

people.name: Ahkari
people.role: leads the caravan Kharjo travels with

unsure.why: Kharjo has no fixed home in the records: he is placed in the open world and his only package is the caravan's wander-near-the-camp package. The caravan's route between cities isn't in these files, so which city camp he is at on a given day isn't known.

The dialogue that sets the first stage isn't in these files and the quest has no start event, so the exact conversation (and any condition on it) can't be read; talking to Kharjo is inferred from him being the quest giver and the objectives naming him.

The dungeon is filled in when the quest starts and isn't fixed in the records. The quest also holds a boss container and a map marker, which points to the amulet sitting in the dungeon boss's chest and the dungeon being marked on your map, but that is read from the quest's slot names, not stated outright.
The quest script pays gold, but the amount isn't in these files. Kharjo is flagged as a possible follower; nothing here ties his recruitment to finishing this quest.

quests.name: The Bonds of Matrimony
quests.plugin: Skyrim.esm (last edited by Unofficial Skyrim Special Edition Patch.esp)
quests.canDoWhy: Once someone agrees to marry you, you arrange the wedding with Maramal at the Temple of Mara in Riften and attend the ceremony.

needs.what: Someone who can marry you agrees to it

starts.how: When a person who can marry you agrees, they tell you to speak to the priest at the Temple of Mara to arrange the ceremony.

starts.where: inside the Temple of Mara, Riften
starts.how: Speak to Maramal about arranging your wedding.

quests.firstStep: Speak to Maramal at the Temple of Mara in Riften about arranging your wedding

takesYou.why: arrange the wedding with Maramal, then attend the ceremony

objectives: Speak to Maramal about arranging your wedding

rewards.when: handled by the quest's script; the records don't say at which point

people.name: Maramal
people.role: priest at the Temple of Mara who arranges and holds the wedding

people.name: the person you marry
people.role: any of about 80 people the records mark as able to marry, such as Ysolda, Mjoll the Lioness, Aela the Huntress, Farkas, Camilla Valerius, Lydia or Brelyna Maryon

unsure.why: The proposal and acceptance lines are not in these files. An amulet mod in the list changes the conditions on several of this quest's lines (adding a check the extract can't name, plus race checks), so whether you must be wearing an Amulet of Mara, or what else a person needs before they'll say yes, can't be read here.
A rejections mod adds lines tied to this quest that let some people turn you down; what decides a refusal isn't readable in these files.

Maramal's packages keep him in the Temple of Mara: breakfast at 7 am, dinner at 3 pm, sleep from 1 am for 6 hours, tending the temple otherwise. One package from the alternate-start mod, checked first, sends him to the Bee and Barb after the opening quest is finished until a short Riften scene there is done, so early on he may be at the inn instead.

The quest has more stages than objectives and none of them have journal text here, so when the ceremony happens, what happens if you miss it, and what follows the wedding (moving in, a shared home) can't be read from these files.
The quest script refers to an Amulet of Mara, but whether it gives one, sells one or takes one isn't shown.
